ei.title: Chapter 6-17 1번: Positive Emotions and Creative Thinking
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: People tend to assume that positive emotions are sources of simplistic or lazy thinking. Think of any highly creative person — such as Vincent van Gogh, Virginia Woolf, T. S. Eliot, or Charles Darwin — and you imagine their creative acts were produced during moments of struggle, tension, gloominess, and even despair. Alice Isen suggested that this view of creativity is wrong — that happiness instead prompts people to reason in ways that are flexible and creative. In her studies, Isen induced positive emotion in her participants with small events. She gave them little bags of candy, or they found a dime she had placed in their path. They watched amusing film clips. These subtle ways of making participants feel good produced striking changes in their reasoning. When given one word (such as carpet) and asked to generate a related word, people feeling positive emotions came up with more novel associations (fresh or texture) than people in a neutral state, who tended to produce more common responses (such as rug). People feeling positive categorized objects in more inclusive ways, rating fringe members of categories (like cane or purse as an example of clothing) as better members of that category than people in a neutral state, whose categories tended to be more narrowly defined.

det.korean: broadly → narrowly: 중립 상태 사람들의 범주가 더 '좁게(narrowly)' 정의되었다.

questions.passage: People tend to assume that positive emotions are sources of simplistic or lazy thinking. Think of any highly creative person — such as Vincent van Gogh, Virginia Woolf, T. S. Eliot, or Charles Darwin — and you imagine their creative acts were produced during moments of struggle, tension, gloominess, and even despair. Alice Isen suggested that this view of creativity is wrong — that happiness instead prompts people to reason in ways that are flexible and creative. In her studies, Isen induced positive emotion in her participants with small events. She gave them little bags of candy, or they found a dime she had placed in their path. They watched amusing film clips. These subtle ways of making participants feel good produced striking changes in their reasoning. When given one word (such as carpet) and asked to generate a related word, people feeling positive emotions came up with more novel associations (fresh or texture) than people in a neutral state, who tended to produce more common responses (such as rug). People feeling positive categorized objects in more inclusive ways, rating fringe members of categories (like cane or purse as an example of clothing) as better members of that category than people in a neutral state, whose categories tended to be more narrowly defined.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 범주를 더 '좁게' 정의한 것은 중립 상태 사람들 → 선지 ③은 주체가 반대라 불일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문 'People tend to assume that positive emotions are sources of simplistic or lazy thinking'과 일치
❌ ② 원문 'little bags of candy ... small events'와 일치
✅ ③ 범주를 더 '좁게(narrowly)' 정의한 것은 '중립 상태'의 사람들이므로 '긍정적 감정을 느낀 사람들'이라는 서술은 불일치 ←정답
❌ ④ 원문 'this view of creativity is wrong'과 일치
det.tip: narrowly defined = 중립 상태 사람들의 범주(긍정 감정 아님)

ch: 어떤 사람들은 긍정적 감정이 단순하거나 게으른 사고의 원천이라고 가정한다.
Isen은 작은 사탕 봉지를 주는 등 작은 사건으로 긍정 감정을 유도했다.
긍정적 감정을 느낀 사람들은 범주를 더 좁게 정의하는 경향이 있었다.
Isen은 창의성에 대한 통념이 잘못되었다고 주장했다.

det.korean: emotions is → emotions are: 주어 positive emotions가 복수이므로 복수 동사 are가 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① emotions is — 원문은 emotions are. 주어 positive emotions(복수)에 맞춰 복수 동사 are가 옳음. is는 수 일치 위반 ←정답
❌ ② induced — Isen induced positive emotion(과거동사), 적절
❌ ③ feel — making participants feel good(make+원형부정사), 적절

det.korean: to reason in ways that are flexible and creative = 유연하고 창의적인 방식으로 추론하도록
det.analysis: prompt + 목적어(people) + to부정사(to reason): 추론하도록 촉발하다. in ways that are flexible and creative = 유연하고 창의적인 방식으로. 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 ways. 총 9단어.
det.tip: prompt A to B: A가 B하도록 촉발하다 / ways that are ~ : ~한 방식
